sentences.en: Hi everyone, in this session I'll be presenting my research about the social history of Britain during the Industrial Revolution.
sentences.zh: 大家好，本次会议中我将介绍我的研究，主题是工业革命时期英国的社会史。

sentences.en: I particularly looked at how ordinary lives were affected by changes that happened at that time.
sentences.zh: 我尤其关注了当时发生的种种变化对普通人生活的影响。

sentences.en: This was a time that saw the beginning of a new
sentences.zh: 这是一个新现象开始出现的时代：

sentences.en: phenomenon: consumerism - where buying and selling goods became a major part of ordinary people's lives.
sentences.zh: 消费主义——购买和销售商品成为普通人生活中重要的一部分。

sentences.en: In fact, it was in the 19th century that the quantity and quality of people's possessions was used as an indication of the wealth of the country.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是在19世纪，人们所拥有的物品的数量与质量被用作衡量国家财富的指标。

sentences.en: Before this, the vast majority of people had very few possessions, but all that was changed by the Industrial Revolution.
sentences.zh: 在此以前，绝大多数人拥有的物品极少，但工业革命彻底改变了这一状况。

sentences.en: This was the era from the mid-18th to the late 19th century, when improvements in how goods were made as well as in technology triggered massive social changes that transformed life for just about everybody in several key areas.
sentences.zh: 这一时期从18世纪中期持续至19世纪末，其间商品生产方式及技术的进步引发了巨大的社会变革，深刻改变了几乎所有人在若干关键领域的生活。

sentences.en: First let's look at manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们来看制造业。

sentences.en: When it comes to manufacturing, we tend to think of the Industrial Revolution in images of steam engines and coal.
sentences.zh: 谈到制造业，我们往往会将工业革命与蒸汽机和煤炭的画面联系在一起。

sentences.en: And it's true that the Industrial Revolution couldn't have taken place at all if it weren't for these new sources of power.
sentences.zh: 的确，如果没有这些新型能源，工业革命根本就不可能发生。

sentences.en: They marked an important shift away from the traditional watermills and windmills that had dominated before this.
sentences.zh: 它们标志着一个重要转变，即从此前占主导地位的传统水车和风车转向了新的动力来源。

sentences.en: The most advanced industry for much of the 19th century was textiles.
sentences.zh: 整个19世纪的大部分时间里，最发达的产业是纺织业。

sentences.en: This meant that fashionable fabrics, and lace and ribbons were made available to everyone.
sentences.zh: 这意味着时尚面料、花边和丝带得以面向所有人供应。

sentences.en: Before the Industrial Revolution, most people made goods to sell in small workshops, often in their own homes.
sentences.zh: 在工业革命之前，大多数人是在小型作坊（常常就在自己家中）制作商品并出售。

sentences.en: But enormous new machines were now being created that could produce the goods faster and on a larger scale, and these required a lot more space.
sentences.zh: 但如今正制造出庞大的新型机器，这些机器能更快、更大规模地生产商品，而这些机器需要大得多的空间。

sentences.en: So large factories were built, replacing the workshops, and forcing workers to travel to work.
sentences.zh: 因此，大型工厂被建造起来，取代了原先的小作坊，并迫使工人前往工厂上班。

sentences.en: In fact, large numbers of people migrated from villages into towns as a result.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大量人口因此从村庄迁移到了城镇。

sentences.en: As well as manufacturing, there were new technologies in transport, contributing to the growth of consumerism.
sentences.zh: 除了制造业之外，交通运输领域也出现了新技术，推动了消费主义的发展。

sentences.en: The horse-drawn stagecoaches and carts of the 18th century, which carried very few people and goods, and travelled slowly along poorly surfaced roads, were gradually replaced by the numerous canals that were constructed.
sentences.zh: 18世纪依靠马匹拉动的公共马车和货运马车，载客和载货量极少，且只能在路况很差的道路上缓慢行驶，后来逐渐被大量修建的运河所取代。

sentences.en: These were particularly important for the transportation of goods.
sentences.zh: 这些运河对货物运输尤为重要。

sentences.en: The canals gradually fell out of use, though, as railways were developed, becoming the main way of moving goods and people from one end of the country to the other.
sentences.zh: 不过，随着铁路的发展，运河逐渐退出了历史舞台，铁路成为将货物和人员从一地运往全国另一端的主要方式。

sentences.en: And the goods they moved weren't just coal, iron, clothes, and so on - significantly, they included newspapers, which meant that thousands of people were not only more knowledgeable about what was going on in the country, but could also read about what was available in the shops.
sentences.zh: 而且，铁路运输的货物不仅包括煤炭、铁制品、服装等，更重要的是还包括报纸——这意味着成千上万的人不仅更了解国内正在发生的事件，还能了解到商店里有哪些商品可供购买。

sentences.en: And that encouraged them to buy more.
sentences.zh: 而这进一步促使他们增加购买。

sentences.en: So faster forms of transport resulted in distribution becoming far more efficient - goods could now be sold all over the country, instead of just in the local market.
sentences.zh: 因此，更快的交通方式使商品分销变得高效得多——商品如今可以销往全国各地，而不再仅限于本地市场。

sentences.en: Audioscripts The third main area that saw changes that contributed to consumerism was retailing.
sentences.zh: 听力原文：第三个发生显著变化并推动消费主义发展的领域是零售业。

sentences.en: The number and quality of shops grew rapidly, and in particular, small shops suffered as customers flocked to the growing number of department stores - a form of retailing that was new in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 商店的数量和质量迅速增长；尤其值得注意的是，小型商店受到冲击，顾客纷纷涌向日益增多的百货公司——这种零售形式在19世纪尚属新兴事物。

sentences.en: The entrepreneurs who opened these found new ways to stock them with goods, and to attract customers: for instance, improved lighting inside greatly increased the visibility of the goods for sale.
sentences.zh: 开设这些百货公司的企业家们找到了新的商品进货方式和吸引顾客的方法：例如，店内照明条件的改善大大提高了待售商品的可见度。

sentences.en: Another development that made goods more visible from outside resulted from the use of plate glass, which made it possible for windows to be much larger than previously.
sentences.zh: 另一项使商品从店外更易被看见的发展，源于平板玻璃的应用，使得橱窗面积远超以往。

sentences.en: New ways of promoting goods were introduced, too.
sentences.zh: 此外，还出现了推广商品的新方法。

sentences.en: Previously, the focus had been on informing potential customers about the availability of goods; now there was an explosion in advertising trying to persuade people to go shopping.
sentences.zh: 此前，宣传的重点在于告知潜在顾客哪些商品有货；而现在，广告数量激增，其目的转为说服人们去购物。

sentences.en: Flanders claims that one of the great effects of the Industrial Revolution was that it created choice.
sentences.zh: 弗兰德斯指出，工业革命的重大影响之一就是创造了选择。

sentences.en: All sorts of things that had previously been luxuries - from sugar to cutlery - became conveniences, and before long they'd turned into necessities: life without sugar or cutlery was unimaginable.
sentences.zh: 过去属于奢侈品的各类物品——从糖到餐具——逐渐变为便利品，不久之后又进一步演变为必需品：没有糖或餐具的生活已难以想象。

sentences.en: Rather like mobile phones these days!
sentences.zh: 这与当今的手机颇为相似！
